title: EFC Phenomenology vs DESI DR2 BAO: A Comparative Fit Analysis
description: This technical note fits a phenomenological dark-energy equation of state w(z), inspired by Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), to seven DESI DR2 BAO measurements using diagonal errors only. The EFC-inspired transition form achieves the lowest chi-squared among models tested (χ2=3.60) versus w0–wa CDM (4.49) and ΛCDM (23.71), providing a necessary but not sufficient consistency check. The work outlines next steps to derive w(z) from EFC field equations and perform multi-probe tests with full covariance.

EFC_inspired_wz.description: Phenomenological EFC-inspired equation of state with a smooth entropy-driven transition near z_trans; fitted post-hoc to BAO.

CPL_wz.description: Chevallier–Polarski–Linder parameterization used for the w0–wa CDM comparison, with DESI-reported best-fit parameters.

key_results.main_finding: Among models tested on DESI DR2 BAO (diagonal errors), the EFC-inspired w(z) achieves the lowest χ2 (3.60), outperforming w0–wa CDM (4.49) and ΛCDM (23.71).
parameters_tested: w0waCDM: w0, wa (DESI DR2 best-fit values)
datasets_used: DESI DR2 BAO DV/rd (7 points; 0.30 <= z <= 2.33; diagonal errors only)

kill_criteria: KC1: A full-covariance joint analysis (BAO + SN + CMB) shows decisive model selection against first-principles EFC (ΔBIC ≥ 10 or equivalently strong Bayes factor) relative to ΛCDM or w0–wa CDM while using comparable priors.

KC2: Solving EFC field equations fails to yield a stable (no ghost/gradient instabilities) background expansion that can realize the phenomenologically required features (phantom-like w < -1 at z ≳ 1 and a smooth transition near z ≈ 1) consistent with causality and energy conditions.

KC3: With DESI DR3/DR4 BAO (full systematics and covariance), the preference for a transition in w(z) disappears and ΛCDM attains a statistically acceptable fit (e.g., p-value > 0.1) with no significant Δχ2 improvement from transition models.
KC4: Combined SN (e.g., Pantheon+ or successor) + BAO + CMB constraints require w(z) ≥ -1 at z > 1 at ≥ 3σ, excluding the phantom-like behavior that the EFC-inspired fit uses to match DESI DR2.

KC5: Early-universe constraints (Planck or next-gen CMB) on the expansion history and sound horizon (r_d) cannot be simultaneously satisfied with the EFC best-fit parameter region while also fitting DESI BAO, leading to a global fit deterioration (e.g., Δχ2_total ≳ 25 relative to w0–wa CDM).

w_early.description: Dark energy EoS at high z

limitations: Post-hoc fitting, not a priori prediction
next_steps: Derive w(z) from EFC field equations

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This T2 technical note shows that a smooth, EFC-inspired transition w(z) achieves a low chi-squared on DESI DR2 BAO (diagonal-only), slightly outperforming CPL and strongly beating ΛCDM, so BAO alone does not disfavor the EFC phenomenology. However, it is explicitly post-hoc and single-probe without covariance, so it does not close any KC or theory gaps; instead it sharpens what EFC must realize from first principles (mild phantom at z>1 and a smooth transition near z~1) and prioritizes multi-probe, full-covariance tests.
graph_insights: This paper adds a direct edge between EFC and DESI DR2 BAO via a transition w(z), linking to CPL and phantom-regime nodes while currently lacking connections to RSD and SN nodes—highlighting the need to integrate growth and multi-probe constraints.

page_updates.new_text: A phenomenological, entropy-driven transition w(z) inspired by EFC yields a good fit to DESI DR2 BAO (diagonal) with χ2=3.60 versus 4.49 (CPL) and 23.71 (ΛCDM). This motivates deriving the same transition from first principles and testing with full covariance across BAO+SN+CMB.
page_updates.reasoning: Summarizes the paper’s result and limitations, aligning with the whitepaper’s evidence hierarchy.

implicit_consequences: First-principles EFC must realize a mild phantom regime at z≳1 and a smooth transition near z≈1 while remaining stable, directly stressing the ADM/Hamiltonian stability program (KC2 interface).
If DR3/DR4 with full covariance remove the transition preference, the EFC-inspired feature would be disfavored, making the planned multi-probe test a high-value falsification path.
The BAO-only improvement suggests potential shifts in r_d and growth history; accelerating the DR2 full-shape RSD verification becomes more critical to cross-check consistency with fσ8.
The result creates a new bridge in the knowledge graph between EFC and mainstream CPL analyses, enabling targeted comparisons and priors in upcoming Bayesian model selection.
Post-hoc nature means no credit as a sealed prediction; subsequent work must convert the functional form into a derived EFC solution with fixed parameters to claim predictive power.
